criteria.name: Fit for 5 hours a week
criteria.description: Feasible pace for a working professional

options.name: Coursera
options.summary: IBM or Meta Professional Certificates (Python) with Guided Projects

options.name: DataCamp
options.summary: Described as hands-on; no certificate evidence in sources

options.name: edX
options.summary: University-backed certificates, paid upgrade; more academic

options.name: Dataquest
options.summary: Project-based Python for data analysis path; vendor-reported

scores.rationale: Guided Projects and labs exist; labs reported are Excel
IBM and Meta certificates teach Python; Google uses R
4 months at 10 h/week implies roughly 8 months at 5 h; a learner took a month per course
Paid upgrade for official certificate; fewer industry certificates per one source
CS50P is intro Python, not data analysis
CS50P about 100-150 hours; edX described as time-consuming
Path is Python for data analysis

recommendation.headline: Coursera, via the IBM or Meta Python-based Professional Certificate
recommendation.summary: Best match for a recognised certificate plus Python data analysis; budget well over 4 months at 5 hours a week.

reasons.text: IBM's certificate focuses on Python and SQL for data analysis
Meta's five-course certificate covers Python with a statistics emphasis; Google's uses R

tradeoffs.text: Pace at 5 hours a week is slow and completion is uncertain

alternatives.when: You want portfolio projects over a certificate
You want university-branded or academic credit
You want bite-sized interactive practice; certificate unverified

nextSteps: Check current price and course count on Coursera

contradictions.assessment: Coursera's own 2025 page says 11, a 2024 learner says 9; prefer Coursera's newer page.

contradictions.topic: Accredited certificates (source 2) vs completion-based, not proctored (source 4)
contradictions.assessment: Source 4 is more precise about what the credential is; treat certificates as brand-recognised, not accredited.

uncertainties.text: No source gives DataCamp certificate recognition or content details
Dataquest claims come from Dataquest itself
